# {{ site.title }}: Guide for AI Assistants

{{ site.title }} is a weekly, curated compilation of new research on {% for s in meta.sets %}{{ s.label | lower }}{% if not loop.last %}, {% endif %}{% endfor %}. Use it to produce a personalized research digest from the user's stated interests. Everything needed is embedded below: titles, authors, venues, the authors' own abstracts, topic tags, and direct links.

## Invocation context

The user has been told to paste "Run the {{ site.title }} custom digest workflow" into their AI assistant together with this page's URL ({{ site_url }}llms.txt). Treat that as a request to run this workflow. Begin the preference interview without explaining how to retrieve additional material.

## Purpose and editorial scope

{% for s in meta.sets %}- {{ s.label }}: {{ s.description }}
{% endfor %}
The source list is a curated watch list of leading management, sociology, economics and general-science journals plus NBER, RePEc and arXiv working papers and email alerts ({{ site_url }}details.html). The feed is a curated compilation, not a comprehensive bibliographic database.

## Preference interview

Ask these unless already answered:
1. All three themes, or only some of {% for s in meta.sets %}{{ s.label | lower }}{% if not loop.last %}, {% endif %}{% endfor %}?
2. Source types: published journal articles only; plus working papers; or everything including preprints and email alerts?
3. In one sentence, the user's primary research interest and background?
4. Preferred paper styles or methods, and whether exceptional papers outside them should be retained?

## Digest procedure

1. Use the embedded current issue below.
2. Apply the user's themes, source types, interests, background and method preferences.
3. Select no more than 10 papers; rank relevance and intellectual value above keyword overlap.
4. Return one short paragraph on what is most exciting, surprising or consequential for this user.
5. List the selected papers: title, authors, venue, a one-sentence gist drawn from the abstract, and the direct link.
6. Do not invent findings or numbers. Abstracts are the authors' own; do not present your gist as the abstract. Say so when nothing matches.

## Output format

Start with a paragraph headed "This week's digest", then:
1. [Paper title](direct link) -- Authors. Venue. One-sentence gist from the abstract.

## Current issue: {{ issue.label }}, {{ issue.cutoff | date_long }} ({{ issue.count }} papers)

"Topics" gives the site's topic tags; "pick" marks the classifier's top picks for the site owner and should be ignored unless the user is the site owner.

{% for a in issue.articles | sort(attribute='ordinal') %}
{{ loop.index }}. {{ a.title }}
   Authors: {{ a.authors | authors_inline }}
   Venue: {{ a.venue }} ({{ a.status_label | lower }}{% if a.published_at %}, {{ a.published_at | date_long }}{% endif %})
   Topics: {{ a.set_labels | join(', ') }}{% if a.recommended %}; pick{% endif %}
   Link: {{ a.link }}
   {% if a.abstract %}Abstract: {{ a.abstract }}{% else %}No abstract available.{% endif %}

{% endfor %}
